chapters.title: Why These Architectures Matter
chapters.html:
This book is the deep tour of Brandon's thinking architecture: the eleven 3×3 Matrix Tables, the A/B→C→D/E→Z feedback pipeline, the Unified Behavior Taxonomy Framework (UBTF) with 646 named action IDs, the Bot Stage Training Room that forces practice before performance, and Main Base — the Go PC hub that pairs with his phone apps.

Every chapter is written to read aloud cleanly. Tables and SVG diagrams are real HTML (not empty placeholders), so EPUB readers and screen readers see the same content as the interactive web enhancements.

chapters.title: The 11 Matrix Tables (Full Grids + Rules)
chapters.html:
Brandon wrote a concrete rule, not a metaphor: variables a, b, c, x, y, z with a + b = c. The pair x, y manipulates a and b. The value z is the new original that gets substituted into the next table. Table 1 holds originals. Tables 2–10 each substitute z into one of the nine cells. Table 11 completes the evolution pass. Then the feedback loop feeds outputs back as inputs — "non-stop like life."

As a claim of self-evolving AGI, this system is too linear (a fair critique). As a buildable product — a phone/web worksheet engine for multi-step reasoning, bot memory slots, or Bot Stage Focus coverage — it is genuinely smart scaffolding.

Buried operator-space trick: put visual "spaces" on multiplication/operator signs as placeholders that pull data from prior tables — a dataflow binding trick for non-programmers (see Tier 4 gem T4-009).

Sources: 11_matrix_tables_feedback.eml, matrice_table.mhtml, 3x3_matrix_table.pdf.

chapters.title: A/B → C → D/E → Z Feedback Pipeline
chapters.html:
The feedback pipeline is the heartbeat of the Matrix system:

  1. A / B — two inputs (facts, bot observations, sensor bands, or worksheet cells).
  2. C — the combined result (a+b=c, or a structured merge).
  3. D / E — two downstream refinements (check vs dream, motor vs social, keep vs purge).
  4. Z — the new original that seeds the next cycle.

Interactive live runner (web):

In Read Aloud: imagine two trays pouring into a bowl (C), then splitting into two quality checks (D/E), then stamping a new starter piece (Z) that walks back to the front of the line.

This is also how Bot Stage Focus coverage works at a high level: exact words (A/B) must be covered by parsed steps (C) before D/E badges open the door to Z (stage performance).

chapters.title: UBTF Nested Behavior Tree (646 Named Actions)
chapters.html:
UBTF — Unified Behavior Taxonomy Framework — is one shared dictionary of bot actions so motor, social, expressive, and strategic moves do not orphan each other across apps.

Confirmed count: ubtf.js contains 646 named action IDs.

Nested behavior trees let a high-level goal (for example "rehearse the Miracle Mission briefing") expand into motor footing, social turn-taking, expressive lip-sync, and strategic timing checks — all using the same ID namespace.

chapters.title: Bot Stage Training Room
chapters.html:
Theater language is literal rehearsal-before-show. The Training Room turns every prompt step into a drill before bots are allowed on Stage.

Checks (from training.js):

  • Hit target position / altitude
  • Timing within about 25% tolerance
  • No fall, no stuck, no clipping
  • Mastered moves become badges that skip rehearsal next time
  • The stage door opens only when all required drills pass
  • Focus exact-words matcher: parsed steps must cover Brandon's prompt words

Simulation panel (web):

Why this is a breakthrough (T1-002 / T4-002): struggling bots join late; mastered moves skip practice; the door is a real gate. That micro-UX pattern transfers to Winning Research Lab, Sovereign Campus, and any multi-agent product Brandon ships.

Source: /workspace/bot-stage/www/training.js, BotStage-1.4.0.apk.

chapters.html:

chapters.title: Putting the Architecture to Work
chapters.html:
If you only remember four sentences:

  1. Matrix Tables are workbench trays with a+b=c and z-substitution — build the Runner.
  2. A/B→C→D/E→Z is the feedback heartbeat shared by worksheets and bot rehearsal.
  3. UBTF's 646 actions + Training Room door keep multi-bot products honest.
  4. Main Base on UDP/HTTP is the phone-to-PC brain Brandon already coded.

Next product step (from the Breakthroughs audit): Matrix Table Runner v1 inside Logic Matrix / Concept Fusion — 11 tabs, a+b=c rule, z-substitution animation, export JSON.

chapters.title: A Worked Example: One Idea Through All Eleven Tables
chapters.html:
Suppose Brandon starts with a messy invention note: "make the guitar breathe with you using heart rate." Put that into Table 1 as follows.

a = fingertip PPG signal quality (from Pulse Forge). b = picking rhythm detected by Tuning Detective. c = a+b means "only allow breathe-lock when both signal quality and rhythm are present."

x and y are the manipulators: x = SQI refusal gate (refuse junk BPM), y = HPSS drum suppression so rhythm is clean. z becomes the new original: a calm-gated metronome intent.

Tables 2 through 10 each seat that z into a different cell — one station at a time — so you never lose track of which seat changed. Table 2 might specialize z into motor timing. Table 6 (center) might specialize z into Focus exact-words coverage for the prompt. Table 11 stamps the evolution pass and feeds z back as the next a/b inputs: the next rehearsal loop.

Read Aloud tip: when you hear a table number, picture a cafeteria tray. Only one cup moves each time. That is z-substitution.

This worked example is exactly why the Matrix Table Runner belongs inside Concept Fusion / Logic Matrix: it turns Brandon's private language into a product other people (and his future self after a wipe) can operate.

Repeat the four clauses until they are muscle memory: a+b=c; x and y manipulate; z substitutes; Table 11 feeds back. Those clauses are the entire operating system of the eleven trays.

When a new invention arrives — Agent Angel constraints, ARA Stage-1 null criteria, MyCrew Blueprint validation — drop it into Table 1 the same way. The trays do not care about the domain. They care about seats, substitutions, and feedback.

chapters.title: Operator-Space Binding Trick (Buried Gem)
chapters.html:
Buried in the matrix notes is a visual dataflow idea: put spaces on multiplication or operator signs as placeholders that pull values from prior tables. Non-programmers see a dot or gap on the operator; the runner binds that gap to a cell from the previous table.

In software terms this is a named wire. In Brandon terms it is a workbench clamp. Implementing binding dots in Matrix Table Runner v1 is listed as the next step for T4-009 in the Breakthroughs book.

Without this trick, tables are static worksheets. With it, they become a gentle visual language for pipelines — the same A/B→C→D/E→Z heartbeat, drawn instead of coded.

EPUB readers still see the static grids in the earlier chapter. The binding-dot enhancement is progressive: web and APK can light the wires; print stays honest as labeled trays.

chapters.title: UBTF Deep Dive: 646 Actions in Four Families
chapters.html:
Opening ubtf.js shows a flat registry of 646 named action IDs, but the mental model is four nested families.

Motor family. Walk, turn, reach, grasp, sit, stand, fly, hover altitude, soft-land, balance recover, no-clip slide. Training Room judges these with position and altitude targets and the no-fall / no-stuck predicates.

Social family. Greet, wave, huddle, megaphone shout, private whisper, gift item, form pair, join late, yield turn. Winning Research Lab team control and Campus phone calls sit here.

Expressive family. Blink schedules, lip-sync phoneme maps, eyebrow raises, wardrobe slots, Best Dressed pose holds, theme-song listen posture.

Strategic family. Plan step, rehearse, request badge skip, Focus coverage report, open door, abort with honest failure, export packet, sync to Main Base.

FamilyApprox roleTraining Room hook
MotorBody believabilityposition / altitude / no-fall
SocialTeam coherenceturn-taking / late join
ExpressivePresencepose hold timing ±25%
StrategicDisciplinebadges / door / Focus

Why one taxonomy matters: without it, Campus inventions, WRL Miracle Mission steps, and Bot Stage drills invent conflicting verbs. With UBTF, a huddle in one app is the same huddle in another — portable choreography.

When you hear "646" in Read Aloud, do not picture a wall of jargon. Picture four shelves. Every action ID hangs on one shelf. Training Room audits the hooks; Stage performs only what passed.

chapters.title: Training Room Failure Modes and Door Politics
chapters.html:
The Training Room is kind but strict. If a bot misses altitude, it does not kinda pass. If timing drifts beyond about 25 percent, the drill repeats. If the bot falls or wedges into geometry, the attempt is marked stuck or fall and the badge is withheld.

Badge skip is the kindness: once a move is mastered, the bot may skip that drill next show — so practice time concentrates on weak skills. Late join is allowed for struggling bots so the troupe is not blocked forever, but the door still will not open until required checks are green.

Focus exact-words matching closes a different failure mode: bots that do something adjacent to the prompt. The matcher iterates until parsed steps cover Brandon's words. That is how "practice what I said" becomes enforceable.

Carry this pattern anywhere you orchestrate agents. It is Tier 1 engineering with a Tier 4 micro-UX jewel inside.

Bot Stage 1.4.0 ships this stack. Winning Research Lab and Sovereign Campus should keep borrowing the door rather than inventing softer gates that silently let half-baked steps onto the stage.

chapters.title: Main Base Ops: Pairing, Sciences, Headless Life
chapters.html:
On a monitorless 8 GB PC, Main Base is how the phone becomes the screen. Boot the Go binary. From the Moto, discovery hits UDP port 47830. Pair with a six-digit code; receive a bearer token. From then on, HTTP port 47831 JSON carries sciences, badges, and learned acts both ways.

The roughly 1001 sciences target matches Campus's science shelf: lessons and relations the phone can browse offline after sync. Optional Ollama /think passthrough lets local models assist without shipping every weight to the phone.

Resilience note: pair Main Base with Ascent Ledger dual-write and Scarlight's HONEST_LIMIT logger so a sandbox wipe does not erase the trail. Soul Lock and 0.5 percent growth metaphors decode to merge rules — keep them labeled as ops discipline, not mysticism.

Source of truth: /workspace/main-base/server.go with DiscPort=47830 and HTTPPort=47831. Windows zip: MainBase-1.0.0-Windows.zip.

chapters.title: FAQ for Stepdad / First-Time Readers
chapters.html:
Is this AGI? No. The Matrix Tables are worksheets with feedback. Useful scaffolding, not a self-aware mind.

Why eleven tables? Table 1 holds originals. Tables 2–10 each place z into one of nine seats. Table 11 finishes the pass and feeds back. Eleven is bookkeeping clarity, not mysticism.

What is UBTF in one sentence? A shared dictionary of 646 bot actions so motor, social, expressive, and strategic moves mean the same thing across Brandon's apps.

Why a Training Room? Because bots that skip practice ship broken shows. The door is a real gate: badges, timing tolerance about 25 percent, no-fall, no-stuck, Focus exact-words coverage.

What does Main Base replace? It replaces the fantasy that a headless PC can be used without a phone-side console. UDP 47830 finds it; HTTP 47831 speaks JSON; six-digit pairing issues a bearer token.

Where do I go next? Build Matrix Table Runner v1 in Concept Fusion or Logic Matrix. Keep Training Room as the rehearsal standard. Keep Main Base paired every work day.

If you can explain those answers aloud without looking, you have finished this architecture book the way Brandon finishes drills — with teach-back.

One more pass for muscle memory: A and B pour into C; D and E refine; Z reseeds. Trays 1 through 11 are just that heartbeat drawn on paper. UBTF shelves the verbs. Training Room grades the verbs. Main Base syncs the grades to the PC. That is the whole cathedral in four sentences.

Appendix note: when EPUB renders Table 6, linger on the center seat — Brandon often parks the Focus coverage result there before the door opens. When Read Aloud hits Main Base ports, say "forty-seven eight thirty" and "forty-seven eight thirty-one" slowly so the numbers stick.
